items.title: Challenges persist despite Hamas backing Gaza ceasefire roadmap
items.description: Hamas has approved the latest draft of a roadmap aimed at completing the implementation of the second phase of the Gaza ceasefire agreement, marking a potential breakthrough in negotiations after more than two and a half years of conflict in the enclave. However, major disputes between Hamas and Israel remain unresolved, particularly over the sequence of key steps, including disarmament, Israel's military withdrawal and Gaza's post-war governance. While Hamas says the transfer of weapons can only take place after Israeli forces withdraw from Gaza, Israel insists that the enclave must be fully demilitarized before any withdrawal. Analysts caution that Hamas' acceptance of the roadmap does not necessarily indicate a fundamental political shift, but rather reflects its attempt to adapt to the realities of the prolonged conflict. They said the agreement's success will ultimately depend on whether all parties can fulfill their commitments during the implementation process. Hamas, Israel make contradictory claims In a statement on Friday, Hamas said it agreed to include discussions on the transfer of heavy weapons within the framework of the Gaza ceasefire agreement, but only on the condition that Israel first ends all forms of military action and withdraws from the Gaza Strip. According to the statement, the conditions include a complete halt to Israeli military operations, the withdrawal of Israeli forces, the entry and assumption of duties by the Palestinian National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) to handle civil functions, the deployment of international stabilization forces, the dissolution of armed groups and militias established by Israel, the launch of reconstruction efforts and guarantees for Palestinian self-determination and an independent Palestinian state. Hamas senior official Basem Naim said on the same day that, after intense negotiations, the group had agreed to the latest version of the ceasefire roadmap. He stressed that Israel must fulfill its commitments under the agreement, while mediators and guarantor countries should take responsibility for monitoring and pressuring Israel to comply with the deal and prevent violations. Israel, however, rejected the proposal, with far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir saying the latest Gaza ceasefire roadmap announced by the so-called "Board of Peace" was "unacceptable." Ben-Gvir argued that a commitment to halt attacks on Hamas members would effectively allow the group to prepare for another assault. The Israeli Prime Minister's Office said a day earlier that the current disarmament plan did not meet Israel's requirements, emphasizing that Israeli forces would only withdraw after Gaza was fully demilitarized. Israeli officials said troops would not pull back from their current positions along the "yellow line" until Hamas achieved "genuine disarmament." Meanwhile, Israeli military operations in Gaza have continued. The Israel Defense Forces said on Friday that recent airstrikes across Gaza had killed two Hamas officials. The military also said it had carried out dozens of operations in the occupied West Bank over the past week, arresting more than 200 Palestinians. Implementation remains the biggest challenge "The proposal does not eliminate the fundamental disagreements between the parties," said Esmat Mansour, a political analyst based in Ramallah. "The most sensitive issues have effectively been postponed to the implementation stage, where they are likely to face their most difficult test." Beyond the dispute over whether withdrawal or disarmament should come first, analysts say the roadmap faces broader challenges, particularly regarding Gaza's future administration and reconstruction. Under the proposed arrangement, Hamas would transfer governance responsibilities in Gaza to a Palestinian national committee. Palestinian analyst Akram Atallah said the committee would face major obstacles, including securing broad Palestinian support, rebuilding administrative institutions and obtaining sufficient funding for reconstruction. Meanwhile, the post-war governance mechanism has also encountered difficulties. The United States announced the establishment of the "Board of Peace" in January to oversee Gaza's transitional administration, but the initiative has faced setbacks. Several US allies, including France, Norway, New Zealand and Italy, reportedly declined to participate. The board has also struggled to secure reconstruction funding, with reports suggesting it had raised less than $1 billion, far below the previously proposed target of $17 billion. In April, reports emerged that the board had yet to enter Gaza due to funding shortages and other obstacles. While Hamas' approval of the roadmap represents an important political step, the coming months will determine whether the understandings reached through negotiations can be translated into lasting arrangements on the ground. Li Zixin, a Middle East expert at the China Institute of International Studies, told China Media Group that the agreement could ultimately fail if it does not clearly define Israel's obligations. "The US-backed phased approach mainly outlines demands on Hamas, while Israel's responsibilities are not clearly specified," Li said. "During implementation, Hamas may accuse Israel of failing to withdraw troops and blocking reconstruction supplies from entering Gaza, while Israel may accuse Hamas of violating the agreement and carrying out attacks. This could eventually lead to renewed fighting and the collapse of the deal." "The real measure of success will not be the announcement of an agreement, but the ability of all parties to implement every stage of it in accordance with their commitments," Mansour said. "Only then can the roadmap provide a genuine opportunity for long-term stability in the Gaza Strip." (With input from Xinhua)

items.title: Banks likely to stay dependent on govt borrowing for profits
items.description: • Limited private sector lending options may persist • Federal govt borrowing from banks rises to Rs5.9tr in FY26 • Private sector receives around Rs1.4tr KARACHI: The country’s banking sector is likely to remain dependent on government borrowing for profits in the current fiscal year as limited private-sector lending opportunities continue to make banks one of the most lucrative sectors for the equity market and investors, financial industry sources said. “The options are limited for lending to the private sector and the situation will remain the same this year as witnessed in FY26,” said a senior banker. Despite a sharp increase in revenue during the last three years, government borrowing also rose rapidly during the period, resulting in almost 50 per cent of revenue going towards interest payments. The Federal Board of Revenue achieved its revised target for FY26, but federal government borrowing from banks rose to Rs5.9 trillion compared to Rs5.4tr in FY25. Bankers said the borrowing trend was likely to continue in the new fiscal year, while the private sector could receive even less credit than it did in FY26. “If investment opportunities appear in the private sector, the situation could change, but policymakers are focusing only on external fronts while relying heavily on banks’ money for rising domestic spending. Their budget always leaves a fiscal gap to be filled by borrowed money or new taxes,” the banker said. Some financial experts pointed to the declining advance-to-deposit ratio, saying it reflected weak private-sector growth. The advance-to-deposit ratio fell to 35.2pc in June 2026 from 38.1pc in June 2025. They said the ratio was among the lowest in the region, contributing to rising domestic debt that consumed around Rs8tr in interest payments. During FY26, the State Bank and the government repeatedly asked banks to boost lending to the private sector, particularly small and medium enterprises, to help lift economic growth from below 4pc. However, the private sector received only around Rs1.4tr compared to Rs5.9tr borrowed by the government. Bankers said nothing had changed in FY27, as neither the manufacturing sector was expected to show a sharp recovery nor the export sector likely to post significant growth. “If domestic investment in the country is the lowest in the region, it clearly indicates that the private sector needs little money from banks,” said S.S. Iqbal, a money market expert. The investment-to-deposit ratio stood at 104.2pc in June 2026, reflecting continued dependence on government securities. Banks remain eager to invest almost all their funds in government papers. The ratio was even higher at 106pc last year. “With growing uncertainties in the region due to the five-month-long war, which is still continuing and spreading, there is little chance for domestic investors to take risks and borrow high-cost money from banks,” Mr Iqbal said. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026

items.title: Parts of Punjab, Sindh face urban flooding risk
items.description: • Tarbela, Mangla levels continue to rise amid monsoon rains • Medium-flood at Guddu and Sukkur barrages; Chenab may reach high-flood at Marala • PDMA says 45 killed in Punjab LAHORE: As the River Indus continues to flow at a medium flood level at Guddu and Sukkur barrages, water levels in the country’s major reservoirs — Tarbela and Mangla dams — have risen significantly over the past 15 days due to torrential rains in their catchment areas. According to reports issued by the Water and Power Deve­lopment Authority (Wapda), the water level at Tarbela dam increased from 1,504.31 feet on July 16 to 1,537 feet on July 31, a rise of 32.69 feet. The reservoir is now just 13 feet below its maximum conservation level of 1,550 feet. Also, the water level at Chashma Lake, which has a total capacity of 649 feet, rose to 648.50 feet on Friday from 646.80 feet on July 16. Similarly, the water level at Mangla dam rose from 1,173.20 to 1,195.55 feet over the same period, while its maximum conservation level is 1,242 feet. Officials attributed the rise in reservoir levels mainly to heavy rainfall in the catchment areas, although snowmelt also contributes significantly to filling Tarbela dam. According to the Flood Fore­casting Division (FFD) of the Met Office, the River Indus at Sukkur would remain at a medium flood level, while flows at Guddu were expected to rec­ede from medium to low flood level over the next 24 hours. It said the Jhelum, Ravi and Sutlej rivers were currently flowing below low flood level. The FFD forecast that the Chenab at Marala, Khanki and Qadirabad would fluctuate between low and medium flood levels and could reach a high flood level at Marala during the forecast period. “Medium to high flows are expected in the nullahs of the Jhelum, Chenab (Dora, Dotta, Dowara, Bhimber, Halsi, Aik and Palkhu) and Ravi (Bein, Basantar, Deg and Sakki). Urban flooding “Flash flooding is expected in the hill torrents of Dera Ghazi Khan, streams in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northern Balochistan, while urban flooding is expected in Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Gujranwala, Sargo­dha, Mandi Bahauddin, Sial­kot, Gujrat, Narowal, Lahore, Okara, Sahiwal and Faisal­abad,” the FFD report said. It also warned of urban flooding, waterlogging and prolonged ponding in Badin, Hyd­erabad, Jamshoro, Khair­pur, Matiari, Mirpurkhas, Sanghar, Shaheed Benazir­abad, Suja­wal, Tando Allahyar, Tando Muhammad Khan, Tharparkar, Thatta and Umerkot. According to Wapda’s daily water report issued on July 31, inflows and outflows at Tarbela on the Indus were 241,000 and 184,300 cusecs, respectively. At Mangla on the Jhelum, inflows were 45,100 cusecs and outflows 7,400 cusecs, while at Marala on the Chenab, inflows were 80,600 cusecs and outflows 66,500 cusecs. Separately, the Provincial Disaster Management Auth­ority (PDMA) Punjab issued a fact sheet on the monsoon and flood situation in Punjab, covering rainfall, river and dam conditions, damage, relief measures and precautionary advice for the public. Rainfall across Punjab According to the PDMA spokesperson, rainfall during the past 24 hours included 75mm in Attock, 67mm in Sialkot, 56mm in Joha­rabad, 46mm in Lahore, 44mm in Sar­godha, 27mm in Khushab, 21mm in Murree, 17mm in Rawalpindi, 15mm in Narowal, and 7mm each in Chiniot and Mianwali. The authority said advance planning, timely deployment of machinery and effe­ctive drainage operations enabled rainwater to be cleared quickly despite heavy rainfall, providing significant relief to residents. The spokesperson said the current spell of monsoon rains was expected to continue until Aug 5. The PDMA, district administrations and other relevant agencies remain on high alert, with continuous monitoring of rivers, dams and barrages. PDMA Director General Saif Anwar Jappa said there was a low flood situation at Kalabagh and Chashma on the River Indus. He said water storage stood at 85pc in Tarbela, 54pc in Mangla, 46pc in Thein dam, 40pc in Pong dam and 37pc in Bhakra dam. According to the PDMA report, 45 people have died and 279 have been injured in rain-related incidents across Punjab during the current monsoon season. Of the fatalities, 33 were caused by the collapse of mud and dilapidated buildings, six by drowning, four by electrocution and two by lightning strikes. Mr Jappa said the injured were being provided the best possible medical treatment and that affected families would be compensated in accordance with the Pun­jab government’s policy. He urged citizens to take precautionary measures during the monsoon, not allow children to bathe in rain drains, low-lying areas, rivers or canals, and to contact the relevant authorities immediately in case of an emergency. According to the PDMA, its control room is monitoring the situation round the clock to ensure a timely response to any emergency. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026

items.title: Govt cuts petrol price by 12 paisas, high-speed diesel by 66 paisas for the next three days
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Friday reduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by 12 paisas and 66 paisas per litre, respectively. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs336.03 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs392.38 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel. The Petroleum Division’s notification said that the new prices would be applicable from August 1 to August 3. Meanwhile, in a bigger price shock, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) notified a record 32pc increase in the price of regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) for August, taking it to $25.83 per mmBtu for SNGPL and $25.09 per mmBtu for SSGCL. This will translate into a retail price of Rs7,204 per mmBtu. The price is based on five imported cargoes from the spot market, as no shipment could be secured from Qatar because of the US-Iran war. This is the single biggest jump in RLNG rates in its decade-long history. This comes on top of an about 15pc increase in the RLNG price fixed last month at $19.52 per mmBtu (Rs5,446 per mmBtu) for SNGPL and $18.63 per mmBtu for SSGCL. Compared with $10.45 (Rs2,916) per mmBtu in February this year, the RLNG price hike works out to around 148pc for August. This mainly results in a substantial increase in fuel costs for power generation. This can be seen from the fact that the fuel cost for RLNG-based power generation in May worked out to Rs31 per unit, compared with Rs13.72 per unit in April. The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan this week. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Naqvi’s remarks ignite fresh debate in political circles
items.description: ISLAMABAD / HYDERABAD / LAHORE: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s call for an overhaul of the country’s governance structur e and the carving out of new administrative units has ignited an animated debate across the country, with the PPP referring the question to its top decision-making forum, the Sindh chief minister flatly rejecting it, Lahore’s lawyers terming it unconstitutional and Sindhi nationalist groups demanding the minister’s resignation. Addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit in Islamabad on Thursday, Mr Naqvi said the present system of governance had collapsed and was fundamentally incapable of resolving the country’s problems. He urged all political parties to sit together and settle every outstanding issue, including the creation of new units and provinces, warning that without structural change the same debates would be taking place a decade from now. He described more administrative units as the only way to bring facilities closer to citizens, said new leadership was needed, and argued that the country’s youth wanted justice, merit and jobs rather than stipends and laptops. PPP refers matter to CEC The PPP’s Central Executive Com­mittee will take up the question of new administrative units, party secretary general Nayyar Bokhari told Dawn , while insisting that the route must be constitutional rather than executive. Bokhari said the Constitution laid down a complete procedure, and that neither new provinces nor any change in provincial boundaries was possible without a two-thirds majority in the relevant provincial assembly, the National Assembly and the Senate. New provinces, he stressed, could not be brought about through an executive order. He said that if there was genuine seriousness about creating new provinces — South Punjab included — the matter should go to parliament and the constitutional requirements should be met. Mr Bokhari called on Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, whose party governs Punjab and the Centre, to begin the process in his own province, recalling that a resolution for a South Punjab province was already pending before the Punjab Assembly. Federal ministers, he said, should raise the issue in the cabinet and, once it was approved, Prime Minister Sheh­baz Sharif should consult PPP Chair­man Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on what he called an important national issue. The CEC would then deliberate, with every decision taken in line with the Constitution, democracy and the will of the people. Responding directly to the interior minister, Mr Bokhari said the proper forum for addressing flaws in the system was parliament rather than the me­dia, and asked who should be held responsible if the system was not working. ‘Sindh will not accept it’ Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah dismissed the proposal as a stereotype that the people of his province would never accept. Speaking briefly to journalists at Bhit Shah on Friday, the chief minister said he had seen the minister’s remarks about the system having collapsed, but was unclear on what exactly Mr Naqvi was referring to. He noted that Shehbaz Sharif was prime minister, that the PML-N governed Punjab, the PPP governed Sindh, a coalition ran Balochistan and the PTI controlled Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. “If he thinks that this system is beyond repair now then he should come up with some proposals,” Mr Shah said. The minister had offered several suggestions, he added, but this particular one — new administrative units or provinces — was “a stereotype which people of this mystic land will not accept”. ‘Unconstitutional’ The Lahore High Court Bar Assoc­ia­tion condemned the interior minister’s statement on changing the governance system, calling it unconstitutional. In a joint statement, LHCBA Presi­dent Babar Murtaza, Vice President So­­­h­ail Qaiser Tarar and Finance Sec­retary Malik Ali Raza Khokhar said those responsible for the destruction of the existing order were now proposing a “new system”. The country’s progr­ess, survival and prosperity, they said, depended solely on strict adherence to the Constitution, the rule of law and complete independence of the judiciary. They criticised the minister for in­­v­i­ting politicians to alter the governance system at a time when, they claimed, popular political leaders and workers had been jailed for prolonged periods on fabricated and baseless charges. The office-bearers demanded the im­­mediate release of all detained political workers and said state institutions and agencies must end their intervention so that constitutional supremacy and judicial freedom could be guaranteed. Call for Naqvi’s resignation Awami Tehreek leaders accused the interior minister of advocating the division of Sindh under the cover of creating new provinces, and demanded that he step down. In a joint statement on Friday, party president Vasand Thari, secretary general Sajid Hussain Mahesar and other leaders said Mr Naqvi enjoyed the PPP’s backing and had, after the MQM and some media organisations, taken up the role of an undeclared spokesperson for the establishment in promoting the new provinces agenda. They said he had lost the moral and political justification to remain interior minister. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026

items.title: France: nouveau mégafeu dans le sud, des milliers d'évacuations
items.description: Un feu de forêt d'ampleur a ravagé vendredi 1.000 hectares dans le département du Var (sud de la France), a indiqué la préfecture qui a ordonné l'évacuation de milliers de personnes des communes en danger. « L'incendie prend de l’ampleur rapidement, renforcé par les rafales de vent. De nouvelles évacuations ont été décidées par les autorités », a indiqué le préfet du Var, Simon Babre, précisant que 2.500 personnes ont été évacuées jusqu’à présent. Lors d'un point de presse, le responsable a expliqué que le feu fixé il y a trois jours a repris à la mi-journée, relevant que « des vents orageux ont attisé les braises encore incandescentes ». Selon le porte-parole des sapeurs-pompiers du Var, le lieutenant Franck Graciano, l'incendie qui s’est aggravé par des sautes de feu en direction de la commune de Montfort-sur-Argens a parcouru 1.000 hectares en moins de six heures. En Gironde (sud-ouest), après plus d'une semaine de lutte des pompiers, la situation reste « toujours stable » sur le front du mégafeu qui a dévasté 42.000 hectares même s'il est encore tôt pour savoir quand l’incendie sera fixé. Dans ce contexte, un total de 308 personnes ont été interpellées dans le pays pour des soupçons d'implication dans des départs et des mises à feu volontaires, avait affirmé plus tôt vendredi le ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez. The post France: nouveau mégafeu dans le sud, des milliers d'évacuations appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: How the Reflecting Pool Vandalism Case Fell Apart
items.description: As government prosecutors examined the Reflecting Pool to build their case against a three-time Olympic canoeist accused of violently ripping the lining with his bare hands, everything fell apart. They found that damage was consistent all around the pool, even in the middle, “where a vandal would not likely attempt to peel the lining.” This evening, the office of U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro asked to drop the case against David Hearn, whom she had excoriated after his indictment 29 days ago. In a striking 19-page legal document filed late this afternoon, her office undermined everything that President Trump has been saying about the damage to the Reflecting Pool for the past six weeks, including the claim that vandals had used a box cutter to slash the floor of the pool. “The damage was the result of a botched installation and not vandalism,” Pirro’s office wrote in a motion to dismiss the case. Taken as a whole, the court filing acknowledged what has been obvious to anyone who has spent time at the Reflecting Pool in recent weeks and watched the president’s $16.4 million project deteriorate in full view. Almost immediately after its reopening in June, the shallow pool filled with the green algae that the expensive renovation was supposed to have prevented. As park workers rushed to combat the algae, the pool’s sealant began to peel away in chunks. It was surprising to see outlined in legal language how Pirro’s office claims it felt duped. Rather than continue with evidence it acknowledged is not there, it is dropping the case. “The Trump administration’s case against Davey Hearn should have never been brought,” his legal team— Norm Eisen , Mary Dohrmann, and Steve Levin—said in a statement. “Its dismissal today does not erase the abuse of government power in arresting and charging a patriotic American who did nothing wrong. The government’s approach was ready, fire, aim. The administration owes Mr. Hearn an apology.” The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Pirro’s office declined to comment beyond what was in the legal filing. [ Read: The canoeist accused of destroying the Reflecting Pool ] The filing largely blamed Department of the Interior officials for supplying information that was used to present evidence to a grand jury and obtain an indictment. Only afterward did prosecutors realize that they had been misled, and that Interior officials “provided less than fulsome information.” A large amount of data and documents that Pirro’s office later received “strongly suggest that a rushed and botched installation” is to blame, her office stated. “These documents indicated a rushed and flawed installation process, with repeated failures of the lining during the installation process, and extensive peeling of the lining throughout the Reflecting Pool,” the filing stated. Eddie Wood—an owner of Atlantic Industrial Coatings, which was paid $14.7 million to line the pool—did not immediately respond to messages. Weather delays hampered installation, the filing stated, and rain meant more delays. Internal notes said that the project was “significantly behind schedule,” which caused further urgency to complete the project before the president’s promised deadline of July 4. A quality-control inspector noted blistering in the finished portions of the liner, requiring further repairs. A final inspection was done on June 9, the filing stated, and crews cleaned the site. But only two days later, on June 11, an engineer at the National Park Service was alerted to peeling in the lining. The fact that officials were scrambling and identifying problems eight days before Hearn was arrested was likely going to cause legal problems in the case. An open question remains as to how and whether the project, one of the most high-profile priorities for the president, will be completed. The pool has been drained, and the latest legal filing indicated uncertainty over why exactly the lining failed in the first place—and whether problems will emerge again when water is pumped back in. I attended Hearn’s court hearings, and they often attracted a crowd of supporters. Some dressed as canoeists; others held signs. At one of his recent hearings, four people wore inflatable-frog costumes. The charges seemed ridiculous to his supporters. But when I recently spoke with Hearn, he told me that the case was hurting his ability to sleep at night. He had once carried the Olympic torch for his country, and he was now worried about being the center of a political firestorm. “It’s unsettling,” Hearn told me, “to feel like I’m being targeted by my government.”

items.title: Trump threatens to hit Iran 'very hard,' Israel expected to join
items.description: US President Donald Trump threatened on Friday to hit Iran "very hard," as US media reported he was considering renewed heavy attacks as soon as this weekend, including against energy infrastructure targets, with Israel expected to join the campaign. After more than five months of war, which began on February 28 when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, there appears to be no end to the conflict, with tit-for-tat attacks resuming. "We'll be hitting him very hard and, you know, at some point they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore,'" Trump said on Friday as he hosted a cabinet meeting at the Camp David presidential retreat in Maryland. The Wall Street Journal later reported that Trump had ordered a fresh attack aimed at convincing Tehran to surrender, which could begin as soon as this weekend, citing unnamed US officials. CBS News, meanwhile, reported that the United States and Israel were planning joint strikes on energy-related targets, possibly throughout the weekend. Such targets would likely include oil refineries and power plants. Trump has repeatedly threatened to strike Iran's vital infrastructure throughout the war, vowing last week to destroy a bridge or power plant every time ships in the vital Strait of Hormuz are attacked. The US president had not yet given the green light for the campaign, but Israel and the US were coordinating, CBS said, citing multiple unnamed sources. The report comes just days after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Washington and met Trump and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Some White House aides voiced strong objections to the plan during the cabinet meeting, the CBS report said. If the plan went ahead, it would mark the first time Israel has joined attacks on Iran since the initial phase of the war.

items.title: RLNG prices rocket to highest level in a decade
items.description: • LPG rates for August increased to Rs254.32 per kg • Ogra says five spot cargoes had to be procured after no shipment secured from Qatar • Regulator finally reveals lower prescribed prices for gas utilities, finalised on June 23 • Rs50bn savings from lower gas rates to be used for circular debt adjustment ISLAMABAD: In a major price shock, Ogra on Friday notified a record 32pc increase in regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) prices for August, fixing the rate at $25.83 per mmBtu for Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) and $25.09 per mmBtu for Sui Southern Gas Company Limi­ted (SSGCL), while denying consumers about Rs50bn in savings from lower natural gas rates. This translates into a retail price of around Rs7,204 per mmBtu. The revised price is based on five imported LNG cargoes procured from the spot market, as no shipment could be secured from Qatar due to the US war on Iran. This is the biggest-ever increase in RLNG prices in the commodity’s decade-long history. The latest increase comes on top of around a 15pc rise in RLNG prices last month, when the rate was fixed at $19.52 per mmBtu (Rs5,446 per mmBtu) for SNGPL and $18.63 per mmBtu for SSGCL. Compared with the February price of $10.45 (Rs2,916) per mmBtu, the RLNG rate for August is around 148pc higher. The sharp increase is expected to significantly raise fuel costs for power generation. The impact is already visible, as the fuel cost for RLNG-based power generation rose to Rs31 per unit in May, compared with Rs13.72 per unit in April. Meanwhile, Ogra also notified a 5.4pc (Rs12.89 per kg) increase in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices for August. It fixed the LPG price at Rs254.32 per kg with effect from Aug 1, compared with Rs241.43 per kg in July. In a belated disclosure, Ogra has revealed that it red­uced the prescribed prices for gas utilities by Rs134 per unit (7.4 per cent), resulting in savings of around Rs50 billion that will be used for circular debt adjustments instead of providing relief to consumers through lower gas prices. For the first time, the regulator did not upload its prescribed price determination, finalised on June 23 and shared with the government, on its website. Since its inception two decades ago, Ogra has publicly released its determinations while simultaneously sharing them with the government. In many cases, it also holds press briefings on its prescribed price determinations and the revenue requirements of gas utilities. However, it remained silent on queries for over a month and finally uploaded the determinations on its website this week after some interveners at public hearings raised concerns. The government has also maintained silence on the matter, although it has already informed the International Monetary Fund (IMF) that consumer-end gas prices would remain unchanged. The savings resulting from lower revenue requirements determined by the regulator for SNGPL and SSGCL would be used to reduce gas sector circular debt, which was last reported at around Rs3.5 trillion, a senior government official confirmed. As a result, Ogra has yet to notify consumer-end gas rates for the current fiscal year, which are required under the law and the IMF programme to take effect from July 1 every year. The fresh determinations would allow annual revenue of around Rs817 billion to the two gas utilities during the current fiscal year, including Rs501 billion for SNGPL and Rs315.8bn for SSGCL. The determinations showed that the prescribed gas price for SNGPL’s revenue requirement was reduced by Rs134 per mmBtu to Rs1,719 for FY2026-27 from Rs1,853 per mmBtu in FY2025-26, resulting in an annual revenue surplus of around Rs46.3bn. “In exercise of its power under section 8(1) of the Ordinance, the Authority, after taking into consideration points raised by interveners, clarifications provided by the petitioner, scrutiny of the petition and available record, provisionally determines the surplus in estimated revenue requirement for the said year at Rs46.279bn,” Ogra stated. It added that the surplus amount would be adjusted against previous years’ shortfall in accordance with the Federal Cabinet’s decision of June 30, 2024, which directed that prior-year shortfalls be adjusted to the extent possible during the current financial year. Accordingly, the regulator determined SNGPL’s estimated revenue requirement, net of revenues, at Rs501.110bn (Rs1,718.96 per mmBtu) for the current fiscal year. Similarly, the prescribed price for SSGCL’s revenue requirement for FY2026-27 was reduced by Rs86 per mmBtu, resulting in savings of Rs2.5bn. Ogra said it had provisionally determined a surplus of Rs1.421bn in estimated revenue requirement for the year. The regulator noted that, based on the currently notified prescribed price, an additional recovery of Rs1.073bn was available, leaving Rs2.494bn for adjustment of previous years’ shortfalls in line with the federal cabinet’s June 30, 2024 decision. Under the decision, the cabinet had directed Ogra to adjust previous years’ shortfalls to the extent of possible surplus during the current financial year. Accordingly, SSGCL’s revenue requirement, net of other revenues, was provisionally determined at Rs315.773bn (Rs1,691.24 per mmBtu) for the current fiscal year, compared with its previous rate of Rs1,777 per unit before June 30, 2026. It may be noted that SSGCL had sought an estimated revenue requirement of Rs1.274 trillion, including Rs545.28bn in unrecovered shortfalls from previous years. Karachi-based SSGCL supplies gas to consumers in Sindh and Balochistan, while Lahore-based SNGPL provides gas to consumers in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026

items.description: Emerse Faé n'est plus le sélectionneur de la Côte d'Ivoire, a annoncé vendredi la Fédération ivoirienne de football (FIF) qui n'a pas renouvelé son contrat. « Le contrat de M. Emerse Faé, sélectionneur de l'équipe nationale A de Côte d'Ivoire, est arrivé à son terme le 31 juillet 2026 et ne fera pas l'objet d'un renouvellement », a-t-elle écrit dans un communiqué. La FIF a salué la contribution de M. Faé au « développement de l'équipe nationale ainsi que les résultats obtenus sous sa direction, qui demeureront une part importante de l'histoire récente du football ivoirien ». Emerse Faé avait été nommé sélectionneur de la Côte d'Ivoire en janvier 2024, après le limogeage du Français Jean-Louis Gasset en pleine Coupe d'Afrique des nations (CAN) organisée à domicile, au lendemain de la lourde défaite des Eléphants contre la Guinée équatoriale (4-0) lors de la phase de groupes. D'abord désigné à titre intérimaire, il avait été confirmé dans ses fonctions le 20 février 2024 après avoir conduit la sélection ivoirienne au sacre continental, après la victoire en finale 2-1 face au Nigeria. Il a ensuite permis aux Eléphants de se qualifier pour la Coupe du monde 2026, où l'équipe a atteint pour la première fois de son histoire le deuxième tour de la compétition, s'inclinant en 16e de finale face à la Norvége (2-1). La Fédération ivoirienne précise qu'elle communiquera ultérieurement sur l'identité du futur sélectionneur ainsi que sur la composition de son encadrement technique. items.title: La FIFA renonce officiellement à son projet de vendre des parts de la Coupe du monde
items.description: La FIFA ne donnera finalement pas suite à son projet de céder des parts des revenus de la Coupe du monde à des investisseurs privés. Dans un communiqué, son président, Gianni Infantino, a annoncé l'abandon de l'initiative FIFA Forward Enterprise, estimant que le projet suscitait trop de divisions au sein de la famille du football mondial. Présentée comme un moyen de renforcer le financement du développement du football, notamment dans les pays les plus modestes, cette initiative visait à créer une nouvelle structure capable d'attirer des capitaux privés. Mais après plusieurs mois de consultations, l'instance dirigeante du football mondial a choisi de faire machine arrière. « Le projet FIFA Forward Enterprise était destiné à fournir une base pour renforcer davantage nos associations membres de la FIFA et notre sport à travers le monde, en particulier dans les pays où le soutien est le plus nécessaire », explique Gianni Infantino. Le président de la FIFA rappelle toutefois que ce projet n'avait vocation à être mis en œuvre qu'avec un large consensus des différentes parties prenantes. « Comme nous l'avons dit dès le départ, [il devait se faire] uniquement si une majorité des associations membres de la FIFA y étaient favorables et toujours sous réserve d'un processus de consultation avec elles, le Conseil de la FIFA, les Confédérations et les parties prenantes plus larges », précise le communiqué. Au fil des échanges, l'organisation a constaté que le projet divisait profondément ses membres. Une situation jugée incompatible avec les objectifs poursuivis. « Ayant écouté attentivement toutes les opinions, il est devenu clair que le projet a créé des divisions d'une nature telle que, indépendamment du niveau de soutien, elles ne servent plus l'objectif initialement fixé », souligne Gianni Infantino. Le patron du football mondial affirme que la priorité de la FIFA demeure l'unité et le développement du football. « Notre objectif a toujours été – et sera toujours – d'unir et d'améliorer. En conséquence, cette proposition ne sera pas mise en œuvre », annonce-t-il. Pour autant, la FIFA ne renonce pas à trouver de nouveaux moyens de soutenir ses fédérations membres. Gianni Infantino indique vouloir poursuivre les discussions avec l'ensemble des acteurs du football afin d'identifier d'autres pistes de financement. « À l'avenir, mon intention est de réunir toutes les parties intéressées dans les jours et semaines à venir dans l'esprit d'un intérêt partagé pour notre sport, et avec l'objectif de continuer à développer le football partout, en particulier dans les pays qui ont le plus besoin de notre soutien », conclut-il. C.G. DIOP

items.title: Thailand: Investigate Online Attacks Against Rights Defenders
items.description: Click to expand Image Angkhana Neelapaijit reports online attacks against her at Bang Yi Reua police station in Bangkok, Thailand, July 31, 2026. © 2026 Private (Bangkok) – The Thai authorities should immediately take effective measures to protect the prominent members of parliament Angkhana Neelapaijit and Romadon Panjor and the human rights defender Anchana Heemmina, all of whom have been facing online death threats and attacks, Human Rights Watch said today. On July 31, 2026, Angkhana, a senator and former member of Thailand’s National Human Rights Commission, filed a complaint with the Bangkok police under the Computer-Related Crime Act that numerous posts on social media accused her of being unpatriotic and sympathetic to the separatist group Barisan Revolusi Nasional (National Revolutionary Front or BRN). Some posts said she should be killed or disappeared. Similar disinformation and hate campaigns were posted on social media against Anchana, founder of the Duay Jai human rights group, and Romadon, a member of parliament from the opposition People’s Party. “The Thai authorities should urgently and impartially investigate online attacks, including death threats, against Angkhana, Anchana, and Romadon, who have been widely recognized for their work defending human rights in Thailand’s deep south,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Those responsible for serious threats should be brought to justice, regardless of their affiliation, to demonstrate Thailand’s commitment to protecting human rights defenders.” Online attacks against Angkhana, Anchana, and Romadon have intensified since the insurgent attack in Ra Ngae district, Narathiwat province, on July 22 that killed five soldiers and injured six civilians. Some of the abusive social media posts come from accounts allegedly affiliated with the Thai government’s information operations. In June, the court of appeal ordered the Internal Security Operations Command to pay Angkhana and Anchana compensation for damages caused by smear campaigns. People who speak out for human rights in Thailand’s deep south—the predominantly Muslim Malay provinces of Pattani, Yala, and Narathiwat, plus Songkhla—where the Thai government has fought the BRN insurgency since January 2004, face grave dangers, Human Rights Watch said. Online attacks appear to have led to real life violence. In March 2004, Angkhana’s husband, human rights lawyer Somchai Neelapaijit, was abducted and his body has never been found. Substantial evidence implicated a group of police officers, who allegedly sought retaliation for Somchai’s involvement in lawsuits regarding widespread police torture of Muslim suspects in the deep south. Over the past 22 years, there have been numerous attacks, including harassment, threats, assaults, enforced disappearances, killings, and unjust prosecutions targeting human rights defenders in the deep south. None of these cases have been successfully resolved by the Thai authorities, including the assassination attempt on Kamonsak Leewamoh, a Muslim member of parliament and prominent human rights lawyer in Narathiwat province in April 2026. The authorities issued arrest warrants for three former military personnel. Human Rights Watch stated in its submission to the 53rd session of the United Nations Universal Periodic Review of Thailand’s human rights record, scheduled for November, that successive Thai governments have failed to uphold their obligations to ensure human rights defenders can carry out their work in a safe and enabling environment, in line with the UN Declaration on Human Rights Defenders. In November 2025, UN human rights experts expressed concern about reports of death threats and online attacks against Angkhana and the Human Rights Watch Thailand senior adviser Sunai Phasuk as a result of their comments regarding possible international humanitarian law violations during the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict. Thailand became a member of the UN Human Rights Council in 2025 and is expected to “uphold the highest standards in the protection and promotion of human rights.” Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul should commit to addressing attacks on human rights defenders and ensure that complaints of threats and harassment are swiftly and independently investigated. The Thai government should send a clear message that threats of violence will not be tolerated, Human Rights Watch said. “Concerned governments and UN agencies should press Prime Minister Anutin to hold accountable those who threaten or attack human rights defenders,” Pearson said. “Thailand should show the world that it has earned its UN Human Rights Council membership.”

items.title: Visas américains : les Guinéens devront désormais déposer leurs demandes à Dakar
items.description: Les procédures d'obtention de visas américains pour les ressortissants guinéens connaissent un changement majeur. À compter du 1er août 2026, l'ambassade des États-Unis à Conakry ne traitera plus les demandes de visas non-immigrants. Les citoyens et résidents de Guinée souhaitant se rendre aux États-Unis devront désormais effectuer leurs démarches auprès de l'ambassade des États-Unis à Dakar, au Sénégal, qui devient le nouveau centre régional de traitement des demandes. Cette mesure s'inscrit dans le cadre d'une réorganisation des services consulaires menée par le Département d'État américain dans plusieurs pays africains. Selon les autorités américaines, cette restructuration vise à centraliser certaines opérations au sein de pôles régionaux afin d'harmoniser les procédures, de renforcer les contrôles de sécurité et d'améliorer l'efficacité du traitement des dossiers. À partir de cette date, les demandeurs guinéens devront donc prendre rendez-vous auprès de l'ambassade des États-Unis à Dakar, s'y présenter pour les différentes étapes requises de la procédure et s'acquitter des frais de visa applicables. Les autorités américaines précisent que cette réorganisation concerne uniquement le traitement des demandes de visas courants et n'affecte pas les autres missions diplomatiques et consulaires assurées par l'ambassade des États-Unis à Conakry. Pour les candidats guinéens au visa américain, cette nouvelle organisation impliquera désormais un déplacement au Sénégal pour accomplir les formalités nécessaires. Washington justifie cette réforme par sa volonté de moderniser la gestion des demandes de visa en Afrique, tout en renforçant les exigences en matière de sécurité et de politique migratoire.

items.title: Fifa scraps controversial World Cup investment plan
items.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino says he has scrapped the controversial plan to sell off stakes in the governing body’s major competitions, following widespread opposition. Infantino said it had become clear the project had “created divisions” that are “no longer in the interest” of its original objective. The Swiss added: “As a result, this proposal will not proceed.” Infantino had offered all 211 member associations $40m (£30m) if they backed a proposal for private investment in its tournaments, including the men’s and women’s World Cups. Infantino on the brink? Who might replace him if he goes? Published4 hours ago European football’s 55 member associations, Uefa, voted on Thursday to boycott World Cups if the plans went ahead. FIFA’s chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said the governing body’s own administration had been “deceived” about the project. Carlos Cordeiro – Infantino’s senior adviser on global strategy and governance – resigned over the matter, saying the proposal was “a bad deal for football” and would “mortgage football’s future”. That came after two other major confederations spoke out against the plans. Concacaf, which governs football in North and Central America and the Caribbean – and hosted this summer’s World Cup – said its members “rejected” the proposal, with sources saying the vast majority of associations from the region are losing, or have lost, faith in Infantino. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said it stood in “solidarity” with Uefa and Concacaf, while UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Infantino was “the wrong man” to lead Fifa. Infantino, 56, is now under immense pressure as he seeks re-election for a fourth term as president at the Fifa Congress in March. He said he now intends to “bring all interested parties back together” in the “spirit of shared interest” in football. Infantino’s plans were unlikely to pass. Despite rejections from Uefa and Concacaf, Fifa initially vowed to continue with its proposals on Friday, saying “nobody is selling football”. However, in announcing the plans had been scrapped, Infantino acknowledged he needed the backing of the majority of Fifa member associations – meaning 106 of its 211 members needed to vote in favour. That became unlikely when the AFC joined Uefa and Concacaf in opposing the plans. Uefa has 55 votes, Concacaf has 35, and Asia has 46. If all member associations backed the stance of their governing body, that would have meant 136 nations voting against Infantino’s plan. The governing bodies in Africa (CAF) and Oceania (OFC) had said they would discuss Fifa’s plan in August. The governing body overseeing football in South America, Conmebol, said it had asked Fifa for “additional information and clarifications” regarding the “scope, structure, governance and possible effects” of the proposals.

items.title: Simandou 2040 : après 4 ans, la CTG dévoile son pari colossal, des milliards d’investissements et des milliers d’emplois pour transformer la Guinée
items.description: La Compagnie du TransGuinéen (CTG) a célébré, ce vendredi 31 juillet 2026 à Conakry, le quatrième anniversaire de sa création sous le thème : « Quatre ans sur les rails de la transformation ». La cérémonie a réuni des membres du gouvernement, des responsables du Comité stratégique de Simandou, des partenaires industriels ainsi que les équipes de la société. L’occasion de faire le point sur les avancées réalisées depuis la mise en place de cette structure stratégique et de réaffirmer les ambitions du projet Simandou 2040. À cette occasion, le directeur général adjoint de la CTG, Dr Moussa Bérété, a retracé l’évolution rapide de l’entreprise en seulement quatre années d’existence. Il a rappelé qu’au début de son aventure, la société comptait moins d’une dizaine d’employés, soulignant qu’il avait eu « l’honneur d’être le premier Guinéen recruté par la CTG ». Aujourd’hui, a-t-il indiqué, la compagnie compte plus de 120 collaborateurs, dont plus de 70 % sont des Guinéens, avec des opérations qui se poursuivent 24 heures sur 24 sur les différents sites du projet. Pour le responsable, cette croissance traduit une véritable culture de performance au sein de la CTG, où la diversité des points de vue est considérée comme un atout pour améliorer la conduite des projets. Il a également insisté sur la mission qui lui a été confiée en matière de contenu local, conformément aux orientations des autorités guinéennes. Selon Dr Moussa Bérété, cette politique repose sur trois axes essentiels : l’accès des entreprises guinéennes aux marchés, la création d’emplois au profit des nationaux et le transfert de compétences et de technologies. Dans cette dynamique, il a annoncé que la CTG prévoit de mobiliser plus de 500 millions de dollars au bénéfice des entreprises guinéennes au cours des trois prochaines années. Sur le plan de l’emploi, il a précisé que les effectifs de la compagnie devraient dépasser 400 employés d’ici à la fin de l’année 2026, avec un taux de guinéisation supérieur à 70 %. À terme, l’ambition affichée est de générer plus de 3 900 emplois directs au profit des Guinéens. Le directeur général adjoint a toutefois reconnu que la montée en responsabilité des cadres nationaux nécessite un processus progressif. Pour accélérer cette transition, la CTG a instauré un mécanisme de transfert de compétences consistant à placer un cadre guinéen en binôme avec chaque expatrié occupant un poste stratégique, afin de préparer sa relève dans un délai d’un à deux ans. Plus de 25 millions de dollars pour les compétences nationales Dans le domaine de la formation, Dr Moussa Bérété a annoncé un investissement de plus de 25 millions de dollars destiné au renforcement des capacités des institutions nationales, au transfert de technologies et au développement des compétences locales. Il a expliqué que la stratégie de la CTG ne se limite pas à attribuer des contrats aux entreprises guinéennes, mais vise également à les accompagner pour leur permettre d’acquérir l’expertise nécessaire afin de participer à d’autres grands projets d’infrastructures en Afrique. Prenant la parole à son tour, le ministre des Mines et de la Géologie, Bouna Sylla, a rappelé les principales étapes ayant conduit à la création de la Compagnie du TransGuinéen. Ancien président du conseil d’administration de la CTG entre juillet 2022 et avril 2025, il a souligné que cette société est née de la volonté du président de la République, le général Mamadi Doumbouya, de fédérer les différents partenaires autour d’un projet stratégique au service des intérêts de la Guinée. Le ministre a évoqué le chemin parcouru depuis les accords signés en mars 2022, la création officielle de la CTG le 27 juillet 2022, les accords de Shanghai en 2023, la convention de co-développement signée en août 2023, la clôture du financement en juillet 2024 et le lancement des opérations le 11 novembre 2025. Pour Bouna Sylla, le contenu local demeure l’un des piliers majeurs du projet, à travers la promotion de l’emploi national, l’ouverture d’opportunités aux entreprises guinéennes ainsi que la formation et le transfert de compétences. Il a également insisté sur la dimension internationale du projet Simandou, qui mobilise des partenaires venus des cinq continents, faisant de cette infrastructure un chantier d’envergure mondiale. Le corridor transguinéen, un levier de transformation économique Représentant le ministre directeur de cabinet de la Présidence de la République et président du Comité stratégique de Simandou, Djiba Diakité, la ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation, Mme Djamy Diallo, a salué les progrès enregistrés par la CTG depuis sa création. Elle a rappelé que le corridor transguinéen constitue désormais l’un des principaux instruments de transformation économique du pays dans le cadre de la vision Simandou 2040 portée par le chef de l’État. La ministre a notamment cité les infrastructures réalisées, dont les 650 kilomètres de voies ferrées multi-usagers, ainsi que les installations portuaires modernes de Moribaya. Celles-ci comprennent deux quais minéraliers capables d’exporter jusqu’à 120 millions de tonnes par an à pleine capacité, ainsi qu’un quai commercial pouvant traiter 2,5 millions de tonnes de marchandises et d’équipements chaque année. Elle a souligné que depuis le démarrage officiel des opérations du corridor, le 11 novembre 2025, la CTG est entrée dans une nouvelle phase avec l’exploitation des infrastructures ferroviaires et portuaires, faisant du corridor transguinéen un véritable moteur de développement économique, d’intégration territoriale et de souveraineté nationale. Mme Djamy Diallo a également rendu hommage aux différents acteurs impliqués dans la réalisation de ce projet, notamment les dirigeants de la CTG, les ingénieurs, techniciens, ouvriers, sous-traitants, administrations publiques, partenaires industriels, collectivités locales et communautés riveraines. En conclusion, elle a estimé que le thème « Quatre ans sur les rails de la transformation » traduit parfaitement l’ambition portée par la CTG, qui dépasse désormais la seule question du transport des minerais et des marchandises pour incarner une vision d’industrialisation, de développement durable et de prospérité partagée. Elle a enfin réaffirmé l’engagement des autorités à poursuivre cette dynamique afin de faire du corridor transguinéen un modèle africain d’excellence, de coopération et d’innovation au service du développement économique et social de la Guinée. À noter que les partenaires de la CTG ne participent pas uniquement à la construction des infrastructures. Ils contribuent également au développement du contenu local, au transfert de compétences et à la création d’opportunités d’emplois pour les Guinéens.

items.title: L’œil de Guinéenews : véhicule sans immatriculation, sans trace : le grand défi de la sécurité routière (seconde et dernière partie)
items.description: Préjudice fnancier Il existe un aspect à signaler dans la non immatriculion des véhicules : c’est le préjudice financier énorme que cette pratique inflige à l’Etat. Tout le monde sait que l’immatriculation est conditionnée par le versement d’un montant proportionnel au type du véhicule et à son usage, mais aussi à certaines autres conditions. L’acquittement de la Taxe Unique sur Véhicule (TUV), de l’autorisation de transport, de l’assurance, de la visite technique sont de celles-là. C’est ainsi que, plus le nombre de sans numéro s’accroît, plus les pertes de l’Etat sont grandes. Incidence sur les statistiques du parc automobile Les statistiques du parc autombile sont indispensables pour maîtriser les besoins réels en importation de carburant, lubrifiant et pièces de rechange. Il en est de même, quand il faut réparer ou construire des routes, etc. Tout projet de développement de ce secteur doit reposer sur des statistiques fiables. Il faut connaître le nombre de véhicules qui circulent sur le territoire national. Aspect sécuritaire Le volet sécuritaire est important à prendre en compte. Pour plein de brigands et autres criminels, rouler sans numéro est un stratagème approprié, pour commettre des forfaitures, sans risquer de se faire prendre. En pareil cas, les bandits font tout pour que les victimes aient toujours affaire à des gens non identifiables, qui ne seront jamais découverts. C'est ainsi qu'ils font en sorte que leurs opérations se terminent toujours par les lamentations des victimes. Quand on entend dire : « les bandits sont partis. Ils étaient dans un véhicule sans numéro. »Cela veut dire que la cause est perdue pour les victimes. Les bandits se sont évadés sans laisser de traces. ils ont littéralement disparu. C‘est la même chose en cas d’accident. Si jamais, on est victime d’un véhicule « sans numéro », il faut alors, prier Dieu que son conducteur soit correct. Sinon, c’est le délit de fuite assuré. Il s’en va et vous laisse, sans aucun moyen pour le retrouver.Mais, il peut aussi arriver qu’il ne fuit pas. Et souhaitons alors qu’il soit solvable et de bonne disposition morale pour vous dédommager. Sinon vous êtes perdant, car un « sans numéro » n’a jamais une police d'assurance pour son véhicule. Toutes les compagnies concluent qu'il est « inconnu du bataillon », comme on le dit, en terme militaire. Une ébauche de solution qui n'a pas fait long feu L a plupart des voitures sans immatriculation sortent des parcs de véhicules d’occasion, surtout la nuit. Pour faire ses courses, en toute liberté, il suffit que l'un des vendeurs le décide. Il prend alors un véhicule sans numéro, en vente, et sort avec, en ville. Pour mettre fin à ce comportement une disposition règlementaire avait été prise dans les années 1980. On avait institué, de commun accord entre la Direction Nationale des Transports Terrestres (DNTT) et les vendeurs de véhicules d’occasion, le port d’une plaque W amovible que tout véhicule d’occasion devait monter avant de rouler en ville, que ce soit pour des besoins d’essai ou autre. Cela a bien fonctionné quelque temps, avant de s’estomper et disparaître. Anarchie et comportements à la limite de l'incivisme Aujourd’hui, on fait du n’importe quoi. C’est l’anarchie totale. Beaucoup d'automobilistes roulent sans immatriculation, d’autres mettent leur nom ou prénoms, un slogan, un surnom ou un sigle sur la plaque. Toutes sortes de bizarreries ! On voit un drapeau étalé sur le tableau de bord, un bérêt, ceinturon, autocollant ou pendentif qui porte : laissez-passer. Peut-être, pour passer les contrôles, sous l'effet d'un trafic d'influence ou tout autre moyen de pression, du genre : « est-ce que tu me connais? Tu sais à qui tu as affaire » ? Sur les motos, on voit des plaques avec AG, PN, GN, sans rien d’autre en plus, etc. Rien de tout cela n’est bon. Ni pour l’intéressé (le propriétaire) ni pour l'Etat. Ne l’oublions jamais, un véhicule sans immatriculation, c’est comme un citoyen sans nom. C’est de l'anonymat; c'est un réel facteur de péril sur nos routes; une grosse perte pour le pays tout entier.

items.title: FIFA scraps World Cup stake sale plans after backlash
items.description: The world football governing body, FIFA, on Friday said it had scrapped plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors after widespread backlash. "Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place," FIFA President Gianni Infantino said on Friday in a statement. The proposal, referred to as the FIFA Forward Enterprise project, will not proceed, Infantino said.

items.title: Violences de Koliagbé : neuf prévenus condamnés à des peines allant de 3 à 10 ans de prison, six relaxés
items.description: Le Tribunal de première instance (TPI) de Kindia a rendu son verdict ce vendredi 31 juillet 2026 dans l’affaire des violences survenues les 17 et 18 mars 2024 à Koliagbé, dans la sous-préfecture de Friguiagbé, sur fond de conflit domanial. Sur les quinze prévenus poursuivis pour incendie volontaire, complicité, destruction de biens privés et vol, neuf ont été condamnés à des peines allant de trois à dix ans d’emprisonnement, tandis que six autres ont été relaxés au bénéfice du doute. Après plusieurs semaines de débats, le tribunal a reconnu cinq prévenus coupables de complicité d’incendie volontaire, de destruction de biens privés et de vol. Ils ont écopé de dix ans d’emprisonnement ferme chacun. Un sixième prévenu, reconnu coupable d’incendie volontaire, de destruction de biens privés et de vol, a également été condamné à dix ans de réclusion criminelle. Deux autres prévenus, poursuivis pour vol et destruction de biens privés, ont été condamnés à trois ans d’emprisonnement ferme. Quant à l’unique femme poursuivie dans cette affaire, elle a été déclarée coupable des mêmes faits et condamnée à trois ans de prison, dont un an assorti de sursis, ainsi qu’au paiement d’une amende de cinq millions de francs guinéens. Les six autres accusés ont, pour leur part, été acquittés au bénéfice du doute, le tribunal estimant que les éléments de preuve à leur encontre n’étaient pas suffisamment établis. Pour rappel, ces violences avaient éclaté après le décès de Naby Camara, survenu alors qu’il était détenu à la maison d’arrêt de Kindia. Des proches du défunt, qui tenaient Ibrahima Kalil Diallo alias « Marcos » pour responsable des poursuites judiciaires ayant conduit à son incarcération, avaient pris pour cible les biens appartenant à la famille Diallo, avec le soutien d’autres habitants de la localité. Les affrontements avaient occasionné d’importants dégâts matériels, notamment l’incendie de trois habitations, de trois véhicules ainsi que d’une plantation appartenant à la famille Diallo.

items.title: WAFCON 2026: South Africa fight back to earn dramatic draw against Côte d’Ivoire
items.description: South Africa staged a spirited second-half comeback to rescue a 2-2 draw against Côte d’Ivoire in Friday’s TotalEnergies CAF Women’s Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2026 Group B clash, keeping their hopes of reaching the quarter-finals alive. Trailing by two goals at the break, Banyana Banyana showed remarkable resilience as Thembi Kgatlana and Hildah Magaia struck in the closing stages to earn a valuable point after a difficult first half. Côte d’Ivoire made the brighter start and nearly broke the deadlock after 15 minutes when Amon Elloh curled an effort just wide of the target. The breakthrough arrived three minutes later through 18-year-old Grace Sery. A swift counter-attack caught the South African defence exposed before the young forward calmly finished beyond Kaylyn Swart with a well-placed strike. South Africa looked for an immediate response and Bongeka Gamede came close in the 20th minute, but her header drifted over the crossbar. The Ivorians doubled their advantage before the interval through the lively teenage star Sery, who completed her brace in almost identical fashion. N’sira Ouedraogo released the teenager with a perfectly weighted lobbed pass, allowing her to race through and finish confidently past Swart. South Africa emerged with renewed purpose after the restart and gradually began to dominate possession as they searched for a way back into the contest. Their persistence was rewarded in the 71st minute when captain Refilwe Jane found Kgatlana, who cut inside before producing an unstoppable strike that gave keeper, Aramatou Diakite no chance. The goal lifted Banyana Banyana and they continued to press for an equalizer. Their reward finally came in the closing moments. With mounting pressure, Ronnel Donnelly headed a perfectly weighted lay-off into the path of Hildah Magaia, who kept her composure to finish clinically and complete South Africa’s impressive comeback. The draw leaves Group B finely poised heading into the final round of fixtures, with the Ivorians in a favorable position with four points, while South Africa’s single point keeps them in contention.

items.title: We should not over-commercialise football – Eric Alagidede
items.description: Football administrator Eric Alagidede has expressed a strong opinion against FIFA’s controversial plans to sell stakes in World Cup competitions to private investors. Fifa wants to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, and external investors will be able to buy stakes in it. It said it would “invite third parties to make minority, non-controlling investments” in a new subsidiary – FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). The plan needs to be passed by a vote of 211 FIFA members. Infantino has written to them saying they will receive $40m (£30m) if they back his controversial proposal. He has set a deadline of 19 September for federations to accept his plans if they want to access an initial $20m (£15m). Speaking to Luv FM, the former Accra Great Olympics General Manager stated that the proposal could lead to over-commercialisation of football. “You cannot commercialise everything and make it so expensive for people to find it is very difficult to watch the game that they love. How many people in the top echelons of our economists actually watch football? “Very few come to Ghana and ask how many bank managers or top-level CEOs go to the stadium on Sundays. Very few of them. So I think we should not over-commercialise football. “Truth also be told: when some of these monies arrive, they will end up not being used for the purposes for which they are meant. So for me, I think it’s something we shouldn’t back. It’s something that would really take a lot away from FIFA. “And you saw how people were complaining about tickets at the last World Cup. The game is for the fans,” he added. On Thursday, UEFA voted to boycott World Cups if the FIFA plan proceeded. Hours later, Concacaf, which hosted this year’s World Cup, released a statement also rejecting the proposals made by Infantino. FIFA President Gianni Infantino had indicated the proposals would need a straight majority to go through – meaning 106 of its 211 members needed to vote in favour of the proposal.

items.title: Violences de Koliagbé : le tribunal de Kindia condamne plusieurs accusés à de lourdes peines
items.description: Le Tribunal de première instance de Kindia a rendu son verdict dans l'affaire des violences survenues les 17 et 18 mars 2024 à Koliagbé, dans la sous-préfecture de Friguiagbé. Les 15 prévenus, poursuivis notamment pour incendie volontaire, complicité, destruction de biens privés et vol, ont été fixés sur leur sort. Au terme de plusieurs semaines de procès, la juridiction a prononcé des peines allant de 2 à 10 ans d’emprisonnement ferme, en fonction du degré d'implication de chaque prévenu. Dans le détail, cinq accusés ont été reconnus coupables de complicité d'incendie volontaire, de destruction de biens privés et de vol. Ils ont chacun été condamnés à 10 ans de prison ferme. Un sixième prévenu, reconnu coupable d'incendie volontaire, de destruction de biens privés et de vol, a lui aussi écopé d'une peine de 10 ans d’emprisonnement ferme. Par ailleurs, deux autres prévenus ont été condamnés à trois ans de prison ferme pour vol et destruction de biens privés. La seule femme poursuivie dans ce dossier a été reconnue coupable des mêmes faits. Le tribunal l'a condamnée à trois ans d’emprisonnement, dont un an avec sursis, ainsi qu'au paiement d'une amende de 5 millions de francs guinéens. En revanche, les six autres prévenus ont été relaxés, le tribunal ayant estimé que les charges retenues contre eux n'étaient pas suffisamment établies. Pour rappel, ces violences avaient éclaté à la suite du décès de Naby Camara, survenu alors qu'il était détenu à la prison civile de Kindia. Convaincus qu'Ibrahima Kalil Diallo, surnommé « Marcos », était à l'origine des poursuites ayant conduit à l'incarcération de Naby Camara, des membres de sa famille, appuyés par d'autres habitants du village, avaient pris pour cible les biens de la famille Diallo. Les affrontements avaient causé d'importants dégâts matériels, avec trois maisons, trois véhicules et une plantation incendiés, tous appartenant à la famille Diallo. Aboubacar Dramé, correspondant régional à Kindia +224 623 08 09 10 L’article Violences de Koliagbé : le tribunal de Kindia condamne plusieurs accusés à de lourdes peines est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Burkina Faso : 124 % de couverture céréalière atteints grâce à l’Offensive agropastorale
items.description: Le ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources Animales et Halieutiques a présenté, ce 31 juillet 2026, le bilan de la mise en œuvre de l’Offensive agro-pastorale et halieutique couvrant la période 2023-2025. Cette stratégie a permis une augmentation historique des volumes de production dans toutes les filières, qu’il s’agisse du riz, du maïs, de l’élevage ou de la pêche. Cette performance repose sur un encadrement étatique renforcé, un contrôle des prix sur les marchés et un taux de couverture des besoins céréaliers du pays qui atteint désormais 124 %. En matière d’aménagement des terres, les réalisations comprennent 11 774 hectares de périmètres irrigués aménagés ou réhabilités, ainsi que 41 275 hectares de bas-fonds, dont 25 031 hectares ont été traités selon l’approche communautaire. Par ailleurs, 120 158 hectares ont été labourés gratuitement ou à prix subventionné au profit des producteurs, et 485 forages à gros débit ont été forés. L’effort d’équipement s’est traduit par la mise à disposition de 1 261 tracteurs, 1 235 motoculteurs, 1 072 matériels de récolte et de post-récolte, 777 semoirs, 1 880 motopompes et 1 545 cages flottantes pour la pisciculture. Pour le transport et le stockage, 37 engins de transport et 418 infrastructures de stockage ont été acquis ou bâtis. Côté transformation et conservation, on dénombre 63 unités de transformation, 398 unités ou kits d’étuvage de riz, 11 chambres froides et une unité de surgélation de poisson. Intensification des investissements Concernant les intrants, le bilan fait état de 160 560 tonnes d’engrais minéraux, dont 70 000 tonnes ont été livrées en 2025 seulement. S’ajoutent 10 665 tonnes de fumure organique, 30 328 tonnes de semences de céréales hors blé, 404 tonnes de semences de blé et 1 771 tonnes de semences de pomme de terre. Les intrants fourragers et alimentaires ne sont pas en reste avec 2 067 tonnes de semences fourragères, 24 684 tonnes d’aliments pour le bétail, 7 825 tonnes pour la volaille et 4 362 tonnes pour les poissons, sans oublier 160,6 millions d’alevins et 87 588 litres de produits phytosanitaires. « Pour ce qui est des investissements, l'Offensive agropastorale et halieutique a été le cadre pour nous d'intensifier les investissements dans le domaine agropastoral et halieutique. C'est vraiment des niveaux d'investissement jamais atteints dans notre pays qui ont été réalisés dans le cadre de l'Offensive agropastorale et halieutique », a indiqué Amos Kiénou, Secrétaire technique de l’Offensive agropastorale et halieutique La lutte contre les épizooties a également mobilisé des moyens considérables. Plus de 9,6 millions de bovins ont été vaccinés contre la péripneumonie contagieuse bovine, plus de 9,2 millions de petits ruminants contre la peste et près de 50 millions de volailles contre la maladie de Newcastle. Par ailleurs, 2,8 millions de petits ruminants ont été protégés contre la pasteurellose et 2,5 millions de poissons contre la streptococcose. Dans le domaine de l’amélioration génétique, 15 912 vaches ont été inséminées, tandis que la contribution du producteur pour cet acte est passée de 50 000 à seulement 5 000 francs CFA. Par ailleurs, 710 vaches gestantes de race performante ont été directement confiées aux éleveurs. En zone pastorale, la reconstitution du cheptel s’est matérialisée par 10 forages, 14 aménagements hydro-agricoles, 11 parcs de vaccination et 3 magasins de stockage de produits vétérinaires, ainsi que par la réhabilitation de 470 hectares de terres dégradées et l’installation de 220 hectares de cultures fourragères. Sur le plan quantitatif, cette dynamique a permis d’atteindre des volumes de production très significatifs. La production céréalière totale dépasse 7,142 millions de tonnes, dont plus d’un million de tonnes de riz paddy et plus de 2,686 millions de tonnes de maïs. La filière piscicole enregistre plus de 58 000 tonnes, tandis que l’aviculture compte plus de 1,8 million de têtes et la pomme de terre plus de 51 000 tonnes. Selon Amos Kiénou, les réformes institutionnelles ont accompagné ces avancées, notamment la création d’organismes spécialisés pour l’approvisionnement en engrais, la gestion des barrages, les produits vétérinaires, la génétique animale ainsi que pour l’alimentation du bétail et des poissons. Réformes institutionnelles Par ailleurs, Amos Kiénou a souligné que la restructuration de la SONAGESS a permis de collecter plus de 300 000 tonnes de céréales, stabilisant ainsi les prix en période de soudure et garantissant l’achat des récoltes locales. « Nous avons vraiment constaté une forte volonté politique des plus hautes autorités du pays de faire de l'agriculture le levier majeur de la transformation structurelle de notre économie. C'est l'occasion pour nous de remercier du fond du cœur les premiers responsables, notamment le camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, qui a mis tous les moyens à disposition de l'Offensive agropastorale pour lui permettre d'atteindre ses objectifs » , a-t-il déclaré. Notons que les réformes institutionnelles et l'accompagnement des producteurs reposent en grande partie sur la création de plusieurs organismes spécialisés. L'État a ainsi mis en place des structures dédiées à l'approvisionnement en engrais avec la SOBIMAP, à la gestion des barrages avec l'ONBAH et aux soins vétérinaires avec le CAMVET. Parallèlement, des entités spécifiques ont été créées pour l'amélioration génétique animale avec la CPAMAP, ainsi que pour la production d'aliments pour le bétail et la pisciculture avec Faso Guulgo. Lazard KOLA Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : 124 % de couverture céréalière atteints grâce à l’Offensive agropastorale est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: GFA should reject FIFA’s World Cup sale proposal – Eric Alagidede
items.description: Football Administrator Eric Alagidede has urged the Ghana Football Association to reject FIFA’s controversial plans to sell stakes in World Cup competitions to private investors. The former Accra Great Olympics General Manager believes that the proposal could lead to over-commercialisation of football, similar to past issues with FIFA. “I think it should be rejected. Look, let’s be very honest with ourselves. Yes, football has become a monetary enterprise. Yes, but I think Gianni Infantino and his cohorts are overstepping their bounds. And if care is not taken, they could go down the way Seb Blatter left FIFA,” he told Luv FM. Alagidede believes the proposal lacks support from key regions like UEFA and North America. “You cannot commercialise everything and make it so expensive for people to find it very difficult to watch the game that they love. How many people are the top echelons of our economists actually watch football? Very few come to Ghana and ask how many bank managers or top-level CEOs go to the stadium on Sundays. Very few of them. So I think we should not over-commercialise football. “Look, you are not going to get a backing of UEFA. They’re not going to get a backing of North America. Look, the only continent that looks likely to back this kind of proposal could be CAF, because clearly you see that member countries need the money,” he stated. He also argued that the funds received may not be used for their intended purposes, which further undermines the proposal’s validity. “Truth also be told: when some of these monies arrive, they will end up not being used for the purposes for which they are meant. “So for me, I think it’s something we shouldn’t back. It’s something that would really take a lot away from FIFA. And you saw how people were complaining about tickets at the last World Cup. The game is for the fans,” he added. On Thursday, UEFA voted to boycott World Cups if the FIFA plan proceeded. Hours later, Concacaf, which hosted this year’s World Cup, released a statement also rejecting the proposals made by Infantino. FIFA President Gianni Infantino had indicated the proposals would need a straight majority to go through – meaning 106 of its 211 members needed to vote in favour of the proposal.
